correctness.rationale: The full matrix is Z diag((omega-1)^|C|) Z^T on the downward-closed Boolean ball, giving the explicit inverse. Its forward all-ones approximation has Frobenius remainder O_r(n^{r-1/2}); the inverse empty-set rank-one approximation has remainder O_r(delta^{-r}n^{r-1/2}). Leading rank-one norms are n^r/r! and delta^{-r}n^r/r!, uniformly in modulus because |omega-1|<=2; multiplying proves the exact asymptotic constant, with no assumption on the growth of m. Numerical inverse and determinant tests were successfully performed for 90 finite cases, independently of the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Sparse Boolean-word Fourier interpolation is a canonical polynomial-dimensional, multivariate deterministic sampling problem. The theorem quantifies the exact reconstruction instability when ambient dimension and character resolution vary on arbitrary coupled scales, not merely a finite computational invariant or an inverse formula already implied by meet-matrix theory. The rank-one localization of worst-amplified data provides structural interpretation; the sharp modulus-uniform constant is the mathematically motivated contribution.
